doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Dizzy's United Nations Orchestra
summary: Moody played in the first version of Dizzy's international band after the tour of Africa, including Mario Rivera, Paquito and Giovanni Hidalgo.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: That must have been particularly exciting for you then when Dizzy put together the whole concept of the United Nations Band. And then that band became a reality and you were a part of it.

I enjoyed it because you had [laughs] – I remember something Dizzy said. I got to say it the way he said it. He said something like, "Three Spanish guys and something four Panamanians and so many Dominican Republicans and four niggers." I mean, he had something like that he'd say. You know, because it was sly. And Steve Toray, Ed Sherry, oh, man. The bass player. Don Lee, Pakito (phonetic sp.). Uh, Rivera. Rivera. What's Rivera (Indiscernible) Saxophone? FEMALE: Mario.

Mario Rivera. Yeah. Mario. Dan Ilo (phonetic sp.). Ignacio Barrera. Yovani (phonetic sp.) Hildago (phonetic sp.). You know. Yeah, so it was nice. I enjoyed that. I was wonderful. Good music and it's even hipper now cause Slide has done some other arrangements on those things. And I've got Antonio Heart, David Sanchez along with the other guys. And who was the bass player? Who was the bass player on that?
So the band has stayed somewhat together? Or –
Somewhat. Yeah, but he's got – No. Pakito has that now. The United Nations.
Yeah.
Now the jazz masters I have now.
Ah. For Slide.
That's it. Yeah. Uh-huh (affirmative).
When did Dizzy come up with the idea the United Nations Band?
I don't know. I really don't know when he came up with that.
But you were on the very first version of that.
I think I was.
Uh-huh (affirmative).
Yeah. I think I was because –
That was in what? Eighty –
I think that's when we came back from the tour of Africa. That's about all of five years ago almost.
Uh-huh (affirmative).
And they built it. Five years. When – FEMALE: It was in January of '89.
January. Yeah, see because when I came back then we got married. Yeah. Yeah.
And that was the band I saw you with at the Greek Theater in Los Angeles in '89.
That's right. And Linda, I mean and Michelle came. My daughter. Yeah.
Uh-huh (affirmative). Yeah, that's a great band.
